scenes.text: A river cuts your village off from the forest. And you need wood.
Swimming across? The current drags you away.
So you chop down a tree, and let it fall across. A bridge!
So you tie ropes between posts, and lay planks across them.
But every step, it sways. And you can never carry anything heavy over it.
So you try stone. But stack stones across a gap, and they just fall in.
Unless you shape them into an arch. Every stone pushes against its neighbors, and the last one in the middle, the keystone, locks them all in place.
Now even a heavy cart can cross.
Then your village grows into a city, and you need to cross a river ten times wider. An arch that big would collapse.
So you build two giant towers, string thick steel cables between them, and hang the road from the cables.
Congratulations. You built a suspension bridge.
The longest one today stretches over two kilometers between its towers.
